root_cause.text: The driver uses the TID value from the IEEE 802.11 header as an index into a fixed-size array without validating that it is within the array bounds, allowing an out-of-bounds access when the TID is >= MAX_TID_COUNT (<9) or > 8 (since array size is 9, indices 0-8).
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (tid < MAX_TID_COUNT)` before accessing `sta_entry->tids[tid]`, and the UBSAN report shows index 10 is out of range for type 'rtl_tid_data [9]'.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses the TID value from the IEEE 802.11 header directly as an index into the tids[] array of size 9 without checking if tid is within bounds (0-8). When tid >= MAX_TID_COUNT (9) or > 8, an out-of-bounds read occurs, leading to a security vulnerability.
